# Recreation Prompt

Create `Reply-All Escape`, a browser-native mobile portrait arcade game based on this prompt: Workplace cringe comedy. A satirical game inspired by The Office with awkward social mini-games, deadpan documentary humor, office politics, lovable incompetence, cringe timing, and mundane-chaos meme energy with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

Mechanics to preserve: two avatar buttons, two mode buttons, a canvas playfield, horizontal pointer/touch movement during play, falling hazards from the top, score increasing continuously, +50 score when tapping hazards in tap-clear mode, fail-on-collision only in avoidance mode, and restart from game over to menu.

Presentation target: satirical office documentary comedy with procedural cubicles, desks, sticky notes, copier/printer props, deadpan lower-third HUD, bold comedy title font, readable mobile panels, a focal rolling-chair office worker, and hazards that visually read as managers, reply-all messages, printer jams, and HR pop-ins.

<!-- Filled v5 source-truth artifact. Keep headings stable. -->
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile portrait canvas arcade dodger with a secondary tap-clear mode
- objective: survive falling social/work hazards as long as possible, or clear hazards by tapping them in the alternate mode
- input model: menu buttons use native taps/clicks; active gameplay uses pointer/touch horizontal movement on the canvas; tap-clear mode also uses pointerdown hit tests on falling objects
- core loop: choose avatar, choose mode, start play, score rises by 0.5 per frame, hazards spawn from the top on a fixed cadence and fall faster as score rises
- fail/friction state: in avoidance mode a distance collision with a falling hazard ends the run; in tap-clear mode collisions shake the screen but do not end the run

## Protected mechanics
- two-step selection flow: avatar then mode
- two mode semantics: slide-to-dodge fail-on-collision and tap-to-clear +50 no-fail-on-collision
- falling hazard spawn cadence: 60 frames in avoidance, 40 frames in tap-clear
- score semantics: +0.5 per animation frame during play and +50 per tapped hazard clear
- distance collision threshold based on player/enemy widths at 0.8 multiplier
- restart returns to menu and clears hazards

## Remixed target
`Reply-All Escape` reinterprets the same mechanics as a workplace cringe documentary. The player is a lovable incompetent office worker scooting through a cubicle floor while managers, reply-all emails, printer jams, HR pop-ins, and mandatory-fun invites fall into their path. The game remains mechanically identical but gains an authored procedural office background, deadpan HUD language, documentary camera framing, mobile-first readable UI, comedy typography, and compact feedback moments.
